sets.dek: The 17th commonest surname in Croatia, and the one this archive is named for. Of the 228 Blaževići it publishes, 59 are joined to the direct line by parent, child and marriage links; the other 169 sit in 32 separate parts of the tree that nothing joins to it. Only the top lane is ours. The three biggest of the others are drawn beneath it from the tree alone, and the dotted join between two of them is one family the tree has entered twice.

sets.note: The tree and the registers say different things about this name, and this page keeps them apart. The tree publishes 228 Blaževići. 59 of them are joined to Hedviga by ordinary parent, child and marriage links: that is the top lane. The other 169 fall into 32 separate parts of the tree that nothing joins to hers. The three biggest are drawn as lanes below it and marked tree only, because no register has been read for them here; the other 29 are listed under the figure. Blažević is the 17th commonest surname in Croatia (7,216 bearers there), densest in counties that are none of this family's, so a shared surname is not evidence of shared descent: the lower lanes and the lists are not “maybe ours”, they are “not shown to be ours”. The only households of the name outside the top lane that a register shows are the Senj ones of 1754–1850, listed apart. The dotted join is one the tree supplies itself: two couples of the 30-person part are entered again, with the same children by name and year, in the 170-person part under other spellings. See Labels Where the Father Should Be, The Same Person, Twice and The Second Name.
sets.owes: For Blažević that is: the parish book of Sv. Jakov Krmpote (named in Toma's death entry and not opened; it should hold Juraj, Anton, Ilija, Grgica and Mateša), which man of Ilija's kin-group fathered Juraj (house 114 places him in the group and cannot go further), Terezija Pećanić's death (in the Senj register that gave Toma's), and, for the lower lanes, one marriage entry each: the tree's own candidates are Ane Blažević (b. 1794) for the 170-person part, a marriage about 1812–1824, and Theresia Cacic (b. 1829) for the 68-person part, about 1847–1859. A register read for Mrzli Dol houses 6 and 30 would say whether the 30-person part and the 170-person part are one family.

nodes.place: Magister Dominicus Uroda (son of the late Georgius)
nodes.why: A «Mr. Domcus [Dominicus?] Vroda» is godfather at Dolac on 27 Jan 1726; godfather («Magister Dominicus Vroda») 1 Jan and 23 Apr 1741; father, with a wife FLORIA, of Lucia (born 12 Dec 1744) and Vittoria (born 10 May 1745); godfather 27 Jun 1749, 20 Mar 1752 and 6 Jul 1755; on 4 Aug 1746 a witness «Dominicus Vrodda, filius Magistri Georgii»; on 13 Feb 1757 «Dominicus filius qd. Georgij Vroda»; on 11 Sep 1757 «Dominicus Vroda Pictor» (a painter); witness at Dolac marriages 11 Jan 1756, 11 Sep 1759 and 10 Aug 1762 and at the cathedral 3 Jun 1767. Two masters of the name seem to be mixed here: a Lucia «ux. q. Mag. Dominici Vrodda», aged about 77, dies on 21 Jun 1746, so an ELDER Magister Dominicus was dead by then; the younger, son of Georgius, has an infant son Paulus buried 7 Jan 1744 — and at the cathedral: Joseph Joannes (born 16 Dec 1739, ceremonies 7 Jun 1740) and Anna (born May 1741; 6 Aug 1741), «filius/filia Magistri Dominici et Florae Vroda», in no Dolac book

ends: **At Šibenik the father is now found: Georgius (b. 6 Oct 1694, d. 17 Aug 1754) was the son of the Magister Dominicus and Lucietta Vroda of the Dolac parish, baptised at the cathedral.** That Georgius died in 1754; Georgius Uroda of Karlobag (ahnentafel 108) was alive from 1763 to 1791, so he is not the Šibenik Georgius — he named his first son Dominicus in 1764, as the Šibenik Georgius did, which keeps the name pattern but proves nothing. Georgius Uroda of Karlobag (ahnentafel 108) named his first son Dominicus in 1764. At Šibenik a Dominicus Uroda, a master, is «filius Magistri Georgii» (4 Aug 1746) and «filius qd. Georgij Vroda» (13 Feb 1757) — a Magister Georgius, alive in 1746 and dead by 1757, and a Dominicus. If Georgius of Karlobag is a son of that Dominicus he is named for his grandfather and his first son for his father; that is a pattern in the names, not a document, and none of the three Dolac baptism books (1685–1762) holds a baptism of him. There was also a Magister Georgius Uroda at Šibenik, married, in 1738: the Georgius of Karlobag cannot be that man if he first fathered a child in 1764, but he could be a grandson or a namesake. The Šibenik Georgius died on 17 August 1754 (aged about 60), so he is not the Karlobag Georgius, who is alive from 1763 to 1791; and the Šibenik Georgius's son Dominicus has only daughters and an infant Paulus in the Dolac books, no Georgius

The dead Dume of Šibenik (d. before 1739) is the one Šibenik Uroda with a recorded child (the bride Simona of 1739); Franciscus, Georgius and Dominicus, masters of the same years, are candidates for his sons, but no register read says so — and the one father named at Šibenik is «Georgius» (1757), not Dume
